A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CCFG research, with a revised title and expanded evaluation in v2. All 14 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v2, including appendices, equations, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MNIST/CIFAR10 class-removal experiments, text-to-image comparisons, and a 10,000-caption COCO evaluation, with additional results in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 reports original class-conditioned and text-conditioned experiments, including ImageNet class pairs, GenEval, DPGBench, PIE-Bench-Neg, and appendix sensitivity and failure analyses.

M1.justification: The core contrastive losses and sigmoid weighting of diffusion predictions remain. v2 Appendix A adds a concrete flow-matching adaptation that applies the weighting to conditional and unconditional velocity differences and advances an ODE through Algorithm 2. This is a limited extension of the existing guidance mechanism.

E1.justification: v2 removes the COCO object-removal benchmark and introduces PIE-Bench-Neg, covering objects, attributes, poses, materials, backgrounds, and styles. It also adds positive-only GenEval/DPGBench evaluation and ImageNet experiments requiring simultaneous attraction to one class and rejection of a visually similar class. SDXL examples already existed in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: v2 adds Perp-Neg and SLD to the retained case-study comparisons, SAFREE to benchmark comparisons, and CFG++ and CFG-zero to positive-guidance evaluations. nCFG is renamed NP, but its stated joint-prompt formula also changes: v1 Equation 8 starts from the positive-conditioned prediction, whereas v2 Equation 9 starts from the unconditional prediction.

E3.justification: For retained MNIST/CIFAR10 experiments, reported sampling changes from 100 to 50 NFE, and CCFG temperature changes from 0.2 to 1.0 and 0.25 respectively; CIFAR10 DNG settings also change. Case studies change from 100 images per case across four cases to 200 across five. New protocols include ImageNet paired-class evaluation, joint alignment/exclusion metrics, aesthetic scoring, and SD3 sampling settings.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's guidance-scale trade-offs and illustrative examples, v2 adds temperature and guidance-strength sensitivity studies with quantitative and visual evidence (Appendix C.3, Figures 6–7). It also introduces explicit multi-attribute and continuous-attribute failure cases (Figure 9) and performance breakdowns by PIE-Bench editing category (Figure 10).

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed identifiers, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bars. Both present point estimates. The increased case-study image counts in v2 change evaluation size, without establishing additional repeated runs or uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: COCO results are removed, and substantial new benchmark results appear. For example, v2 Table 1 reports SD1.5 GenEval overall scores of 0.432 for CCFG, 0.407 for CFG, and 0.426 for CFG++. Results do not show universal superiority: SDXL PIE-Bench-Neg VLMall is 0.8120 for CCFG versus 0.8128 for SLD. Retained class and case-study results also change under revised settings, preventing direct version-to-version performance comparisons.

T1.justification: v2 replaces v1's small-step DDPM mean approximation with a stochastic-DDIM formulation in the CCFG derivation. Appendix A adds an ODE-to-SDE marginal-equivalence argument for flow matching, while Appendices C.2–C.3 add the explicit loss gradient, temperature–variance relationship, and limiting behavior. The earlier posterior-mean equivalence derivation is retained in Appendix C.1.

C1.justification: The central claim of contrastive attraction/repulsion with quality-preserving concept suppression remains. v2 adds an explicit comparative claim that its negative guidance operates independently of positive prompts, unlike several competing refinements (Section 3.2). Positive guidance receives greater emphasis, although that capability was already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive qualifications: multi-attribute prompts may be only partly suppressed, subtle continuous attributes can yield borderline failures, and removing attributes of positively requested objects is especially difficult. It also explains temperature-dependent failure behavior. The missing closed-form sampling distribution remains an acknowledged limitation, and v1's discussion of negative prompting across dataset complexities is retained in Appendix B.1.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility information: classifier checkpoint links, DiT-XL/2 resolution and ResNet50 weights, the WordNet class-pair construction procedure, category-specific PIE-Bench-Neg construction instructions, and SD3 sampling details. Its hyperparameter table covers more methods and models. The VLM evaluation prompt is revised, while the COCO prompt-generation instructions disappear with that experiment.

R1.justification: v2 replaces the dedicated safety/unlearning discussion with broader positioning against empirical negative-prompt refinements and attention-based guidance. It explicitly distinguishes CCFG's standalone applicability and probabilistic motivation, discusses attention manipulation as complementary, and adds relevant work including SAFREE, CFG-zero, and attention-guidance methods. These changes extend beyond bibliographic publication updates.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is substantially rewritten around positive-only, negative-only, and combined guidance. Related-work sections are reorganized, the former main-text discussion moves to Appendix B, and the appendices are restructured into extensions, discussion, analyses, and experimental details. Terminology changes from nCFG to NP, alongside title and author-list revisions.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is extensively redesigned. v1's overview and toy-distribution figures are merged into v2 Figure 2; objective plots move beside the algorithm in Figure 3. Case-study tables give way to aggregate bar charts, benchmark tables expand, and new sensitivity, failure, and category-analysis figures appear. The teaser and appendix layouts also change substantially.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important weaknesses in v1's validation through broader comparator coverage, direct positive-guidance evaluation, parameter sensitivity studies, and explicit failure analysis. Fuller derivations and implementation details also improve assessability and reproducibility. Reporting weaknesses remain: Section 4.1 misstates Perp-Neg's ranking relative to Figure 4, and uncertainty reporting is still absent. These limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in evidence and characterization of the method's boundaries.
